newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold prices rise, volume eases.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold prices rise, volume eases.

text.p: Prices firmed on Istanbul's gold exchange on Wednesday in lira terms but no trade was done in dollar terms for the second day in a row.
Traded volume fell to 691 kilos from 702 kilos on Tuesday. Gold closed 800 lira up at 1,144,000 lira per gram.
Traders said they preferred to trade gold in lira terms because of comparatively cheaper prices and uncertainty in world markets where gold prices remained in a narrow range.
The last dollar trade was on Monday morning when gold ended at $380.30 an ounce.
Most of the turnover was in the first session at 526 kilos.

"Demand was firmer in the morning because gold prices were higher in the free market than on the exchange. But prices climbed on the exchange in the afternoon as the lira weakened on the interbank," a dealer said.

Banks, the main sellers on the exchange, convert their gold prices according to interbank lira/dollar rates while foreign exchange and gold shops, the main buyers, use the cash dollar rates set in the free market.
The lira ended weaker at 93,175 against the dollar on the interbank versus Tuesday's 92,865. --Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 08 75
